glossary.Psychological distress: Emotional suffering such as worry, low mood or fear that affects daily life.
glossary.Personality traits: Lasting patterns of thinking, feeling and behaving that make up a person's character.
glossary.Impairment: Reduced ability to function normally in work, relationships or daily activities.
glossary.Restlessness: Inability to stay still or relax, often with fidgeting.
glossary.Irritability: Being easily annoyed or quick to anger.
glossary.Muscle tension: Muscles staying tight or contracted, causing aches, often in the neck and shoulders.
glossary.Palpitations: An unpleasant awareness of one's own heartbeat, which may feel fast, strong or irregular.
glossary.Tremor: An involuntary rhythmic shaking, usually of the hands.
glossary.ECG: Electrocardiogram: a recording of the heart's electrical activity from electrodes on the skin.
glossary.Substance misuse: Harmful use of alcohol or drugs.
glossary.Functional impairment: Difficulty carrying out normal roles such as work, study or self-care.
glossary.Chronic stress: Long-lasting activation of the body's stress response, which harms health over time.
glossary.Mimic: A condition that produces similar symptoms and can be mistaken for another.
glossary.Acute: Coming on suddenly and over a short time.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: measures haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: a blood test of kidney function and salts such as sodium and potassium.
glossary.Anaemia: A low haemoglobin level, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
glossary.Clinical assessment: Diagnosis made from history, examination and mental state, without a confirmatory test.
glossary.Baseline tests: Tests done at the start to rule out other causes and to compare against later.
glossary.Self-guided help: Structured self-help materials worked through by the patient with minimal therapist contact.
glossary.Psychoeducational groups: Group sessions teaching people about their condition and coping skills.
glossary.Suicidal ideation: Thoughts about ending one's own life.
glossary.Somatic symptoms: Physical bodily symptoms, such as a racing heart, caused or worsened by a mental state.
glossary.Dysregulation: Abnormal control of a system, so it is over- or under-active.
glossary.Threat perception: How readily the brain judges a situation to be dangerous.
glossary.Sympathetic activation: Switching on the fight-or-flight nervous system: raised heart rate, sweating, tension.
glossary.Peripheral: Towards the edges of the body, such as the hands and feet.
glossary.Synaptic: At the synapse, the tiny gap where one nerve cell signals to another.
glossary.Downregulation: A cell reducing the number or sensitivity of its receptors after prolonged stimulation.
glossary.Limbic system: Brain structures including the amygdala that process emotion and fear.
glossary.Paradoxical: The opposite of the expected effect.
glossary.Beta-adrenergic: Relating to beta receptors stimulated by adrenaline and noradrenaline, which raise heart rate.
glossary.Tachycardia: A heart rate above 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Cognitive: Relating to thinking, such as worrying thoughts.
glossary.Withdrawal: Unpleasant symptoms when a drug the body has adapted to is stopped.
glossary.Hypocalcaemia: A low blood calcium level, causing tingling and muscle cramps.
